title: Nested loops and patterns

youtube.title: C++ Nested Loops: Star Patterns and Tables | C++ Programming EP 20
youtube.description: In this episode you will put one loop inside another, print a star triangle and print a grid of numbers, with Xecxec the crab. 0:00 Intro · 0:15 Nested loops and patterns · 0:49 A star triangle · 1:29 Rows and stars · 1:59 Second program · 3:00 Recap · 3:35 Bug of the Day · 4:23 Challenge · 4:43 Next episode

thumbnail.visual: big text "STAR PATTERNS" in tomato on cream; Xecxec next to a triangle made of stars; thin black border and drop shadow.
thumbnail.pose: Xecxec next to a triangle made of stars

scenes.animation: Tomato title card: EP sticker thuds in, title stamps with a whoosh, Xecxec scuttles in and waves; thud, whoosh, claw-click, sting
scenes.narration: Today we put a loop inside a loop. With it, you can print triangles, grids and tables.

scenes.onScreen: "Nested loops and patterns": numbered lines (1. The inner loop runs fully for each outer round; 2. Rows use the outer loop; 3. Columns use the inner loop) and an analogy card: a clock: the minute hand loops many times for each step of the hour hand
scenes.animation: Lines spring in one by one with a pop; the analogy card slides in from the right
scenes.narration: A nested loop is a loop inside another loop. For each round of the outer loop, the inner loop runs from start to finish. We use the outer loop for rows, and the inner loop for columns. Think of a clock. The minute hand goes all the way round for every small step of the hour hand.
points: The inner loop runs fully for each outer round

analogy.title: Nested loops and patterns
analogy.body: A clock: the minute hand loops many times for each step of the hour hand

scenes.onScreen: triangle.cpp: two loops print a triangle of stars
scenes.animation: Code types in with key-tick; butter [HL n] highlight sweeps line by line with marker-swipe; explanation card on the right
scenes.narration: [HL 5] The outer loop counts the rows, from one to four. [HL 6] The inner loop prints one star for each count up to the row number. [HL 7] Row one prints one star. Row two prints two stars. [HL 9] After each row, endl moves to the next line. The result is a triangle.

scenes.onScreen: a table: row number and the stars printed
scenes.animation: Table rows slide in one by one; the row the narrator mentions glows butter
scenes.narration: Here is each row. The inner loop runs as many times as the row number. That is one star in row one, and four stars in row four. The line break comes after the inner loop ends.

diagram.caption: a table: row number and the stars printed

scenes.onScreen: grid.cpp: a three by three table of products
scenes.animation: Second program or a twist on the first; [HL n] and [TRACK name=value] cues drive the variable tracker; output panel fills line by line with a ding per line
scenes.narration: [HL 5] The outer loop gives the row r. [HL 6] The inner loop gives the column c. [HL 7] Each cell shows r times c. [TRACK r=2] In row two, the cells are two, four and six. [HL 9] The line break ends each row.

scenes.animation: Dark-blue terminal: the compile command types with key-tick, the run command types, output prints in mint with a ding
scenes.narration: Save the file as grid dot cpp. Compile it with g plus plus. Then run the program. The program prints a grid with three rows. The last row shows three, six and nine.

scenes.animation: Recap lines tick in one by one with a pop; Xecxec nods after each tick
scenes.narration: Let us recap. One. A nested loop is a loop inside a loop. Two. The inner loop runs fully for each round of the outer loop. Three. Use the outer loop for rows and the inner loop for columns. Four. Print the line break after the inner loop. Pause the video. Say these ideas out loud, one time, slowly.
points: A nested loop is a loop inside a loop.
The inner loop runs fully for each round of the outer loop.
Use the outer loop for rows and the inner loop for columns.
Print the line break after the inner loop.

scenes.onScreen: BUG OF THE DAY: A missing line break
scenes.animation: Butter banner drops in with a buzzer; the program runs and the wrong output appears in tomato; the fix slides in and the output turns mint with a ding
scenes.narration: Bug of the Day. We want a triangle. The program prints ten stars in one long line. The line break is after both loops. It runs only once. Move endl inside the outer loop, after the inner loop. Then each row gets its own line.

scenes.onScreen: I printed a triangle of stars. It was a very sharp piece of code.
scenes.animation: Full tomato screen, card flips in with a rimshot, Xecxec snaps his claw
scenes.narration: I printed a triangle of stars. It was a very sharp piece of code.

scenes.onScreen: Task card: print a number triangle
scenes.animation: Task card pops in; checklist ticks with a pop; Xecxec holds a tiny pen
scenes.narration: Your challenge: Print a triangle of numbers. Row one prints the number one. Row two prints the number two, two times. Go up to row four. Write your answer in the comments.

scenes.animation: Next-episode card slides up with a whoosh; right side stays empty for end-screen elements; sign-off text types in
scenes.narration: We end module two here. Next time: functions, the building blocks of every program. Keep coding, says Xecxec!

bug.error:
Program output (it runs, but the answer is wrong):

**********
bug.why: The line break sits after both loops, so all ten stars go on one line. It must run once per row, inside the outer loop.

pun: "I printed a triangle of stars. It was a very sharp piece of code."
challenge: Print a triangle of numbers. Row one prints the number one. Row two prints the number two, two times. Go up to row four.
challengeAnswer: Use two loops. In the inner loop, print the row number instead of a star. Print endl after the inner loop.
